PAPERS.title: Long-term O(3) and PM(2.5) exposure and dynamic progression of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: A longitudinal cohort study.
PAPERS.short: Shenzhen 493,388 adults: PM2.5 HR 1.054 per IQR (5.0 ug/m3) for CKM-syndrome progression; O3 the steadier signal
PAPERS.pm: Preceding-365-day mean PM2.5 and O3, updated at each risk interval; per IQR (PM2.5 5.008 ug/m3, O3 7.431 ug/m3); exposure source not stated in abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Nonfatal forward progression of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages
PAPERS.affil: Shenzhen Center for Chronic Disease Control, China; Shenzhen Center for Chronic Disease Control, China
PAPERS.n: Shenzhen Healthy Aging Research Cohort, 2018-2024: 493,388 participants, 1,029,004 risk intervals and 162,083 forward CKM-stage transitions; multistate Cox models with time-updated 365-day mean exposures. Per IQR of PM2.5 (5.0 ug/m3), HR 1.054 (95% CI 1.030-1.078) for overall progression, 1.073 (1.030-1.118) for early (to stages 1-2) and 1.055 (1.027-1.085) for advanced (to stages 3-4). O3 per IQR (7.4 ug/m3) gave larger and steadier HRs (overall 1.151, 1.138-1.165); PM2.5 estimates moved with model specification in six-pollutant and common-sample analyses. Weakness: progression is defined by examination-visit staging, so visit frequency (itself tied to health-seeking) shapes event capture; exposure model unnamed in the abstract. Relevance: the PM2.5 signal is specification-sensitive at a 5 ug/m3 contrast, i.e. within typical uncorrected low-cost-sensor error.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposure to the general external exposome and incidence of ischemic heart disease in Europe: a meta-analysis of 14 cohorts.
PAPERS.short: 14 European cohorts, >29 million people: IHD incidence +1.4% per quartile PM2.5 in administrative cohorts; adult cohorts positive but non-significant
PAPERS.pm: Residential PM2.5, PM10, NO2 plus built-environment exposome (greenspace, blue space, imperviousness, walkability); per one-quartile increment; time-varying
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident ischemic heart disease
PAPERS.affil: Karolinska Institutet, Sweden; not stated
PAPERS.n: Eight traditional adult cohorts and six administrative cohorts from 11 European countries, >29 million participants, 464,386 incident IHD cases; time-varying Cox models for single exposures and quantile g-computation for domains, random-effects meta-analysis by cohort type. In administrative cohorts a one-quartile increment was associated with IHD incidence +1.4% (95% CI 0.8-1.9%) for PM2.5, +0.9% (0.1-1.7%) for PM10 and +1.7% (1.0-2.4%) for NO2; the air-pollution domain jointly +2.5% (1.9-3.1%). Adult cohorts, which carry individual confounder data, gave positive but non-significant estimates. Weakness: the significant estimates come from administrative cohorts with the thinnest confounder control (no smoking, BMI), and a quartile increment differs in ug/m3 across countries. Relevance: effects of this size need exposure contrasts resolved at the scale of address-level models; sensor networks can validate within-city gradients those models smooth.

PAPERS.title: Critical windows of gestational exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) and pregnancy loss in New Jersey, United States.
PAPERS.short: New Jersey 1.18 million conceptions: weekly PM2.5 lowers live-birth-identified conceptions, RR 0.993 per 10 ug/m3 at gestational week 21
PAPERS.pm: Population-weighted county weekly PM2.5 from modelled air-quality data; per 10 ug/m3; lags from LMP to week 40
PAPERS.endpoint: Pregnancy loss, proxied by weekly counts of live-birth-identified conceptions (LBIC)
PAPERS.affil: Yale School of the Environment, USA; Yale School of the Environment, USA
PAPERS.n: Time-series of weekly live-birth-identified conceptions (LBIC) in all 21 New Jersey counties, LMP dates 2000-2016 (n = 1,179,217 births), quasi-Poisson DLNM over gestational weeks 0-40, adjusted for trend and meteorology. Higher weekly PM2.5 reduced LBIC counts (i.e. more loss); the strongest lag was week 21, RR 0.993 (95% CI 0.990-0.995) per 10 ug/m3. Assuming 10-50% of conceptions are lost, a 10 ug/m3 increase across weeks 0-40 implies 5.2 (3.9-6.6) to 9.3 (7.1-11.9) losses per 1,000 conceptions per week. Weakness: losses are inferred from missing births, so conception-rate shifts and fertility timing are indistinguishable from loss; county-weekly modelled PM2.5 is coarse. Relevance: weekly windows are exactly where county averages fail and residence-level sensing would sharpen exposure.

PAPERS.title: Long-term exposures to low concentrations of fine particles (PM(2.5)) from vehicular exhausts and residential wood combustion and the incidence of dementia and Alzheimer's disease.
PAPERS.short: Helsinki FINRISK 5487 adults at ~1 ug/m3 source-specific PM2.5: no dementia association for traffic exhaust (HR 0.95 per 0.1 ug/m3); wood-combustion HRs elevated but imprecise
PAPERS.pm: Dispersion-modelled residential PM2.5 from vehicular exhaust (mean 1.06 ug/m3) and residential wood combustion (0.45 ug/m3); 3-15-year averages; per 0.1 ug/m3
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident dementia and Alzheimer disease (registers)
PAPERS.affil: University of Eastern Finland, Finland; University of Eastern Finland, Finland
PAPERS.n: FINRISK participants from Helsinki and Vantaa (surveys 1992-2012, n = 5,487) followed to 2022 in registers; 601 incident dementia and 500 AD cases; Cox models with modelled source-specific outdoor PM2.5 at the address. Means were 1.06 ug/m3 (SD 0.95) from vehicle exhaust and 0.45 (0.21) from residential wood combustion. Per 0.1 ug/m3, dementia HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.85-1.05) for exhaust and 1.23 (0.79-1.92) for wood combustion, the latter consistently above 1 across models; no AD associations. Weakness: exposure contrasts of tenths of a ug/m3 are at or below dispersion-model error, and ~600 cases cannot resolve modest HRs. Relevance: source-resolved contrasts this small are beyond any optical sensor; wood-smoke specificity needs composition (levoglucosan, BC-type) rather than mass.

PAPERS.title: Predicting personal PM(2.5) exposure among community-dwelling older adults using multi-source environmental, residential, and behavioral information.
PAPERS.short: Fuzhou 247 adults >=60, 72-h personal PM2.5: Bayesian LASSO R2 0.48, RMSE 19.3 ug/m3; passive smoking +16.2 ug/m3 the largest predictor
PAPERS.pm: 72-h personal PM2.5 with concurrent outdoor PM2.5; questionnaire residential, behavioural and time-activity predictors
PAPERS.endpoint: Personal PM2.5 exposure prediction
PAPERS.affil: Fujian Medical University, China; Fujian Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: 247 community-dwelling adults aged >=60 in Fuzhou wore personal PM2.5 monitors for one 72-h session (summer or winter) with concurrent outdoor PM2.5 and questionnaire predictors; Bayesian LASSO. Bayesian R2 0.481 (95% CrI 0.412-0.539), RMSE 19.26 ug/m3 (18.80-19.88). Predictors with CrIs excluding zero: passive smoking only +16.2 ug/m3 (7.9-24.5), current smoking +12.9 (7.0-18.8), residence near a major road +7.4 (0.7-14.2), outdoor PM2.5 per SD +6.5 (3.8-9.4); directions stable across repeated cross-validation. Weakness: one 72-h session per person, so within-person seasonal variability is confounded with between-person predictors; monitor type and its humidity correction are not given in the abstract. Relevance: outdoor PM2.5 explains less of personal exposure than tobacco smoke at home - the argument for wearable or indoor sensors over ambient-only assignment in older cohorts.

PAPERS.title: Public health and economic burden of a proposed 3500-MW natural gas plant in Virginia: A PM(2.5) dispersion and impact analysis.
PAPERS.short: Proposed 3500-MW Virginia gas plant: ~326.5 t/yr primary PM2.5, >1.2 million people exposed, USD 30.5-65 million/yr health damages; project withdrawn
PAPERS.pm: Plant-attributable PM2.5 from emission factors of comparable turbines, InMAP dispersion; COBRA health and valuation
PAPERS.endpoint: Plant-attributable PM2.5 health and economic burden
PAPERS.affil: Politecnico di Milano, Italy; Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, USA
PAPERS.n: Health impact assessment of a proposed 3,500-MW natural-gas plant (Pittsylvania County, Virginia) driven by data-centre demand: emissions from operating data of comparable turbines, dispersion with InMAP, health and valuation with EPA COBRA. Estimated ~326.5 tons/yr of PM2.5 raising exposure for >1.2 million people in Virginia and North Carolina; >17,600 county residents would see increments >0.1 ug/m3 over a ~8 ug/m3 background. Annual health-related damages USD 30.5-65 million, falling disproportionately on older, lower-income and racially marginalised communities; the project was withdrawn after the findings were disseminated. Weakness: reduced-form InMAP and COBRA's national concentration-response functions, no uncertainty beyond the damage range, and secondary PM from NOx is handled only through InMAP chemistry. Relevance: increments of 0.1 ug/m3 are far below what any monitor can verify after construction; impact is modelled, never measured.

PAPERS.title: Examining the Association between Particulate Matter (PM2.5) Exposure and Under-five Child Mortality in India Using Cluster-Level Analysis
PAPERS.short: India NFHS-5 clusters: under-five mortality AOR 1.07 per 10 ug/m3 PM2.5; 1.40 above 80 vs below 40 ug/m3 (preprint)
PAPERS.pm: Satellite-derived (NASA) global annual mean PM2.5 linked to NFHS-5 survey clusters; per 10 ug/m3 and categories
PAPERS.endpoint: Under-five mortality
PAPERS.affil: University of Gour Banga, India; Mamta Health Institute for Mother and Child, India
PAPERS.n: Research Square preprint. NFHS-5 (2019-21) births linked at cluster level to NASA satellite-derived annual mean PM2.5; bivariate LISA for spatial clustering and survey-adjusted multivariable logistic regression. Each 10 ug/m3 PM2.5 was associated with adjusted OR 1.07 (95% CI 1.04-1.10) for under-five death; clusters above 80 ug/m3 vs below 40 ug/m3 gave AOR 1.40 (1.17-1.67), with marked spatial heterogeneity. Weakness: one annual PM2.5 value per cluster for deaths spanning five years before the survey, cross-sectional design, and the Indo-Gangetic gradient in PM2.5 tracks poverty and health-system access that survey covariates only partly capture; not peer-reviewed. Relevance: rural India is where satellite products carry the least ground truth - the case for low-cost sensor co-location to anchor these surfaces.

PAPERS.title: Citywide re-evaluation of the Bangkok air quality health index: classification performance, nonlinear same-day respiratory associations, and implications for precautionary health communication.
PAPERS.short: Bangkok AQHI vs 23-hospital OPD 2021-24: poor classifier (AUC 0.35-0.54); same-day respiratory RR 1.023 at AQHI 7 vs median
PAPERS.pm: Bangkok AQHI (fixed original coefficients, multipollutant) from city monitoring; PM2.5 comparator; AQHI 7 vs citywide median
PAPERS.endpoint: Daily outpatient respiratory, asthma, COPD and ischaemic-stroke morbidity
PAPERS.affil: Mahidol University, Thailand; Phramongkutklao Hospital, Thailand
PAPERS.n: City-wide time series of outpatient visits at 23 hospitals across 26 postcodes, 1,461 days in 2021-2024; the Bangkok AQHI applied with its original fixed coefficients; ROC analyses for high-morbidity days, negative binomial models per IQR and DLNMs over lags 0-7. Discrimination was poor: fixed-direction AUC 0.353-0.539 for the AQHI and 0.421-0.562 for PM2.5. No consistent log-linear association; DLNMs found a small same-day association at AQHI 7 vs the median for clinically selected respiratory morbidity, RR 1.023 (95% CI 1.004-1.042), surviving Bonferroni and FDR correction; cumulative lag 0-7 associations near null. Weakness: OPD counts include COVID-era service disruption, and many outcome definitions invite multiplicity despite correction. Relevance: an index built from sparse regulatory monitors classifies poorly city-wide; denser sensing is one test of whether exposure misclassification explains it.

PAPERS.title: Ambient particulate chemical components and dengue incidence: A 10-year nationwide study in Thailand.
PAPERS.short: Thailand 77 provinces 2012-2021, 837,616 dengue cases: MERRA-2 dust PM2.5 positively, OC, BC and sulfate inversely associated with incidence
PAPERS.pm: Monthly MERRA-2 reanalysis dust PM2.5, organic carbon, black carbon and sulfate by province
PAPERS.endpoint: Monthly provincial dengue incidence
PAPERS.affil: Khon Kaen University, Thailand; Khon Kaen University, Thailand
PAPERS.n: Ecological analysis of 837,616 dengue cases reported across 77 Thai provinces, 2012-2021, against monthly MERRA-2 aerosol components; Bayesian spatial INLA models adjusted for demographic and temporal factors. Dust PM2.5 was positively associated with dengue incidence, while organic carbon, black carbon and sulfate were inversely associated; the abstract reports no effect sizes or credible intervals. Weakness: ecological province-month design in which aerosol components co-vary with season, rainfall and burning, all of which drive Aedes ecology; MERRA-2 composition at province scale is a reanalysis product with no local validation; mechanism is speculative. Relevance: composition-resolved inputs for disease early warning cannot come from mass-only low-cost sensors; at most they supply total PM2.5 for local calibration of the reanalysis.

PAPERS.title: The associations of outdoor and indoor air pollution with cognitive function among older adults in China.
PAPERS.short: CHARLS 8806 adults >=60: higher outdoor PM1/PM2.5/PM10 and solid-fuel cooking (global cognition beta -0.57) precede poorer cognition, stronger in rural residents
PAPERS.pm: Annual mean PM1, PM2.5 and PM10 (source not stated in abstract); household solid fuel for cooking and heating
PAPERS.endpoint: Global cognition, memory and mental status, 2013-2020
PAPERS.affil: Wuhan Mental Health Center, China; Wuhan Mental Health Center, China
PAPERS.n: 8,806 CHARLS participants aged >=60, 2013-2020; linear mixed-effects models of 2013 exposures on later cognition, stratified by urban-rural residence. Higher outdoor particulate matter was generally associated with poorer subsequent global cognition and memory; 2013 PM2.5 was inversely associated with global cognition in both 2015 and 2018 (coefficients not given in the abstract). Solid-fuel cooking in 2013 predicted lower 2018 global cognition (beta -0.57, 95% CI -0.93 to -0.22), memory (-0.53, -0.77 to -0.31) and mental status (-0.23, -0.40 to -0.06); heating fuel gave similar estimates. Associations were stronger in rural participants. Weakness: household fuel is a binary proxy with no measured indoor PM, attrition in an older cohort is likely exposure- and cognition-related, and outdoor PM effect sizes are not reported. Relevance: rural indoor combustion is where measured personal exposure is thinnest and cheap sensors most informative.

PAPERS.title: Prenatal exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and heating-season air pollution: associations with birth outcomes in a coal-reliant city.
PAPERS.short: Urumqi 279 mother-infant pairs: longer heating-season gestational overlap linked to shorter birth length (-0.011 cm per day); PAHs detected in 47-91% of plasma samples
PAPERS.pm: Gestational overlap with the municipal heating season; ambient PM2.5 and PM10; 16 PAHs in maternal and cord plasma (GC-MS)
PAPERS.endpoint: Neonatal anthropometry (length, weight, Ponderal Index)
PAPERS.affil: Xinjiang Medical University, China; Xinjiang Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: 279 mother-infant pairs enrolled June 2019-January 2020 in Urumqi, a coal-heated city; long vs short gestational overlap with the heating season; 16 PAHs by GC-MS in paired maternal and cord plasma. Detection rates were 66-91% in maternal and 48-78% in cord plasma. Longer heating-season exposure was associated with lower birth length (p = 0.002) and Ponderal Index but not birth weight (p = 0.132); each additional day of heating-season overlap was associated with -0.011 cm length (p = 0.004); higher gestational PM2.5 and PM10 also tracked shorter length. No CIs reported. Weakness: heating-season overlap is collinear with season of birth, small n, and enrolment over seven months confounds exposure with calendar time. Relevance: winter coal-heating peaks are steep and spatially patchy - the setting where home-level sensors would replace a seasonal proxy.

PAPERS.title: Mendelian randomization study reveals the effects of air pollution on the risk of male and female infertility.
PAPERS.short: Two-sample MR (UK Biobank exposures, FinnGen outcomes): genetically predicted PM2.5 nominally raises male infertility (p = 0.04), not after Bonferroni; nothing for female infertility
PAPERS.pm: Genetic instruments for PM2.5, PM2.5-10, PM10, NO2 and NOx (UK Biobank address-based exposures)
PAPERS.endpoint: Male and female infertility (FinnGen)
PAPERS.affil: Second Affiliated Hospital of Jianghan University, China; Second Affiliated Hospital of Jianghan University, China
PAPERS.n: Two-sample Mendelian randomisation using instruments for five pollutants from UK Biobank and male and female infertility from FinnGen; four MR estimators plus heterogeneity and pleiotropy tests. Genetically predicted PM2.5 was associated with male infertility at p = 0.04, which did not survive Bonferroni correction; no associations for NOx, NO2, PM10 or PM2.5-10 with male infertility, and none for any pollutant with female infertility. No effect sizes are given in the abstract. Weakness: SNPs associated with a residential pollution estimate index where people live (ancestry, SES, migration), not biological susceptibility, so the exclusion restriction is implausible; the headline result is a nominal p-value. Relevance: none to measurement; it illustrates why genetic proxies cannot substitute for exposure data.

PAPERS.title: Modifiable and Context-Specific Factors Associated with Dementia in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Community-Derived Cross-Sectional Study
PAPERS.short: DR Congo 721-person cross-sectional sample: poverty, low resilience and depression associated with dementia; PM2.5 not associated (medRxiv)
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 one of 16 social, behavioural and environmental factors (source not stated in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Dementia status (including suspected Alzheimer disease)
PAPERS.affil: Emory University School of Medicine, USA; University of Navarra, Spain
PAPERS.n: medRxiv preprint. 721 participants in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (232 cognitively unimpaired, 489 with dementia including 247 suspected AD); logistic regression on 16 factors with age, sex and missing-category indicators. Adding the factors raised Nagelkerke R2 from 0.106 to 0.368. Poverty (aOR 2.34, 95% CI 1.52-3.60), low resilience (1.84, 1.18-2.86) and depression (1.53, 1.02-2.31) were associated with dementia; higher education inversely (0.51, 0.39-0.66 per SD). PM2.5 exposure was not significantly associated; no estimate is given. Weakness: cross-sectional, non-representative and dementia-enriched sampling, mean imputation, and an unnamed PM2.5 source in a region with almost no ground monitoring. Relevance: Central Africa has near-zero reference monitoring; a null here says more about exposure data than about PM2.5 and dementia.

PAPERS.title: Global inequalities in subarachnoid hemorrhage attributable to temperature extremes and air pollution among adults over 40 years: Insights from the GBD study with projections to 2050.
PAPERS.short: GBD 2021, adults 40+: ambient PM the largest environmental contributor to subarachnoid-haemorrhage deaths (50,936 in 2021), projected 65,847 by 2050
PAPERS.pm: GBD 2021 ambient particulate matter, household air pollution, high and low temperature risk factors
PAPERS.endpoint: Subarachnoid haemorrhage deaths and DALYs attributable to environmental risks
PAPERS.affil: Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, China; Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, China
PAPERS.n: Secondary analysis of GBD 2021 for adults aged 40+ in 204 countries: SAH burden attributable to ambient PM, household air pollution and temperature extremes, trends 1990-2021, ARIMA and exponential-smoothing projections to 2050 and decomposition. In 2021 ambient PM accounted for 50,936 SAH deaths and 1,357,090 DALYs, more than household air pollution (32,224 deaths) or low temperature (18,648). Ambient-PM-attributable deaths rose from 35,329 in 1990, while household-air-pollution deaths fell from 77,441; projections reach 65,847 ambient-PM deaths by 2050. Burden was higher in males. Weakness: GBD attributable estimates inherit its exposure surfaces and integrated exposure-response curves; the SAH-specific relative risk is borrowed from stroke evidence; no uncertainty intervals in the abstract. Relevance: none directly; GBD surfaces in low-income regions are the least validated by ground sensors.

PAPERS.title: Liriopesides B ameliorates fine particulate matter-induced lung injury by directly targeting ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2 Q2 to dismantle the macrophage lactylation-neutrophil extracellular trap axis.
PAPERS.short: Mouse PM2.5 lung injury: macrophage glycolysis and lactylation drive neutrophil extracellular traps via UBE2Q2/LDHA
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 exposure in mice; dose and particle source not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5-induced lung injury; macrophage lactylation and neutrophil extracellular traps
PAPERS.affil: Chengdu Institute of Respiratory Health, Southwest Jiaotong University, China; Chengdu Institute of Respiratory Health, Southwest Jiaotong University, China
PAPERS.n: Mechanistic study combining single-cell RNA sequencing, surface plasmon resonance, docking and a macrophage-depleted adoptive-transfer mouse model. PM2.5 reprogrammed pulmonary macrophages towards a hyper-glycolytic, lactylation-driven state that paracrinally drove neutrophil chemotaxis and extracellular-trap formation; the E2 enzyme UBE2Q2 acted as the checkpoint regulating LDHA to sustain the cascade, and a plant-derived inhibitor of that axis reduced injury. No exposure-response relationship and no effect sizes with CIs are reported. Weakness: laboratory PM2.5 of unstated origin and concentration, so no dose can be mapped to ambient exposure; the mechanism rests on a single pathway readout. Relevance: none to measurement, but lactylation as an intermediate would need composition-resolved exposure, not mass alone.

PAPERS.journal: Environmental science and pollution research international
PAPERS.title: Model pollution iron-rich silica particulate: impairment of glutamate/GABA balance and ROS generation in brain nerve terminals.
PAPERS.short: Synthetic iron-rich silica core-shell particles raise extracellular GABA and glutamate in rat synaptosomes, size- and dose-dependently (0.1-1.0 mg/ml)
PAPERS.pm: Synthesised Fe3O4@SiO2 core-shell nanoparticles characterised by TEM, SEM, DLS, SAED and XRD; 0.1-1.0 mg/ml
PAPERS.endpoint: Extracellular glutamate and GABA levels and ROS generation in rat brain nerve terminals
PAPERS.affil: L. V. Pisarzhevskii Institute of Physical Chemistry, National Academy of Sciences, Ukraine; same institute, Ukraine
PAPERS.n: Model multipollutant iron-rich silica particles (Fe3O4@SiO2 core-shell, varying constituent proportions) applied to isolated rat brain synaptosomes at 0.1-1.0 mg/ml. Extracellular radiolabelled glutamate and GABA rose with particle size and dose, GABA being the more sensitive readout; the particles reduced spontaneous, H2O2- and kainate-induced ROS generation, interacted with the synaptosomal membrane and added to the effects of Cu2+, Pb2+ and Cd2+ rather than mitigating them. No CIs are reported. Weakness: milligram-per-millilitre doses of synthetic particles are orders of magnitude above realistic deposited lung or brain doses, and synaptosomes bypass every biological barrier. Relevance: supports interest in the iron fraction of ambient PM, which optical sensors cannot see at all.

PAPERS.title: Exposure to Diesel Particulate Matter Aggravates Developmental Toxicity Induced by Cyclophosphamide in Rats.
PAPERS.short: Rat co-exposure: diesel particulate matter aggravates cyclophosphamide-induced fetal abnormalities and delayed ossification, not uniformly dose-dependent
PAPERS.pm: Diesel particulate matter administered to pregnant rats alongside cyclophosphamide; doses not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Embryo-fetal development; maternal hepatic oxidative-stress markers (MDA, CAT, SOD)
PAPERS.affil: Chonnam National University, Republic of Korea; Chonnam National University, Republic of Korea
PAPERS.n: Pregnant rats received cyclophosphamide with or without concomitant diesel particulate matter; endpoints were maternal toxicity, fetal weight, morphological alterations and ossification, plus hepatic malondialdehyde and catalase and superoxide-dismutase activities. Cyclophosphamide alone reduced maternal and gravid uterine weight, fetal and placental weight and hepatic antioxidant activity. Added diesel PM aggravated several fetal abnormalities and ossification delay and further lowered maternal catalase and SOD, though responses were not uniformly dose-dependent. No CIs are reported. Weakness: a co-exposure design with a potent chemotherapeutic cannot isolate a PM effect size, non-monotonic responses suggest few animals per dose, and the administration route is not stated. Relevance: none to monitoring; it is an interaction-screening result.

PAPERS.title: Lysosome-associated oxidative signals and membrane permeabilization contribute to intracellular ROS accumulation and alveolar epithelial cell death induced by zinc oxide nanoparticles
PAPERS.short: Zinc oxide nanoparticles kill alveolar epithelial cells through lysosomal lipid peroxidation and membrane permeabilization; NRF2 is protective
PAPERS.pm: Zinc oxide nanoparticles by oropharyngeal aspiration in mice and in alveolar epithelial cells; doses not stated in the abstract
PAPERS.endpoint: Alveolar epithelial cell death, lysosomal membrane permeabilization and oxidative stress
PAPERS.affil: not stated; not stated
PAPERS.n: Oropharyngeal aspiration of ZnO nanoparticles raised pulmonary 4-hydroxynonenal and activated NRF2 in mice, with greater injury and lysosomal change in the alveolar than the bronchial compartment. In vitro, uptake was clathrin- and cholesterol-dependent with lysosomal trafficking; the particles increased lysosomal lipid peroxidation, altered CALPAIN1 and mature CTSB/CTSD and permeabilized lysosomal membranes. N-acetylcysteine and a CTSB inhibitor attenuated injury, while Nrf2 silencing worsened it. No exposure-response or CIs are reported. Weakness: engineered-nanoparticle doses are not anchored to ambient or occupational concentrations, and the comparison across lung compartments is qualitative. Relevance: metal-oxide ultrafines are invisible to optical mass sensors; the relevant exposure metric here is surface area or number.

PAPERS.title: Relationship between PM2.5 exposure during wildfires and acute angle-closure: a self-controlled case series.
PAPERS.short: Wildfire PM2.5 and acute angle-closure, self-controlled case series (metadata only)
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Wildfire-period PM2.5 (per title); exposure source not stated
PAPERS.endpoint: Acute angle-closure episodes (per title)
PAPERS.affil: Stanford Medicine, USA; Byers Eye Institute, Stanford, USA
PAPERS.n: Metadata only. The title indicates a self-controlled case series relating PM2.5 exposure during wildfires to acute angle-closure (BMJ Open Ophthalmology, Stanford). No abstract reached the index at issue time, so no finding is asserted. Relevance: a self-controlled design needs daily exposure at the patient address, which during fires varies over kilometres and hours - the regime where regulatory monitors are sparsest and sensor networks or smoke models carry the exposure. Priority recheck when indexed.

PAPERS.title: Atmospheric polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon emissions, multimedia fate, and human health risk assessment in Punjab Province, Pakistan (2015-2024): a bottom-up emission inventory approach.
PAPERS.short: Punjab, Pakistan bottom-up PAH inventory 2015-2024: emissions up 32.8% to 5287 t/yr, domestic coal 53.1% of the total
PAPERS.pm: Bottom-up inventory of 16 USEPA priority PAHs by source and fuel, Monte Carlo uncertainty (10,000 iterations); multimedia fate and health-risk assessment
PAPERS.endpoint: PAH emissions, multimedia fate and human health risk
PAPERS.affil: not stated; not stated
PAPERS.n: First source-resolved bottom-up PAH emission inventory for Punjab Province, 2015-2024, built from official Pakistani activity statistics and compiled emission factors with Monte Carlo uncertainty propagation. Total PAH emissions rose from 3,981.5 t in 2015 to 5,287.3 t in 2024 (+32.8%), with no sign of the policy-driven inflection seen in comparable Chinese provinces; domestic coal combustion contributed 53.1% and petroleum combustion 25.7%. Weakness: emission factors are transferred from other countries to Pakistani fuels, stoves and kilns, activity data are provincial aggregates, and the multimedia fate and risk layers compound those uncertainties without validation against measured ambient PAH. Relevance: particle-bound PAH is a combustion-source marker no mass sensor resolves; an inventory of this kind is only testable against filter or online composition measurement.

PAPERS.title: Behavioural and social determinants of ambient air pollution exposure: an umbrella review.
PAPERS.short: Umbrella review of 18 reviews: time outdoors raises individual exposure, while greenspace, advisories, race and socio-economic status shape community exposure
PAPERS.pm: Ambient air pollution exposure as the outcome of behavioural and social determinants; no single PM metric
PAPERS.endpoint: Determinants of ambient air pollution exposure
PAPERS.affil: Queen's University, Canada; Health Canada, Canada
PAPERS.n: Umbrella review of five databases (searched November 2024) covering 18 reviews, with JBI quality appraisal and thematic synthesis, aimed at informing refinement of air quality indices such as Canada's AQHI. Determinants sorted into behaviour (physical activity, travel, protective action) and society (public health, urban planning, neighbourhood and housing, social identity) across 17 subthemes. Time spent outdoors was associated with higher individual exposure; greenspace, public-health advisories, race and socio-economic status shaped community-level exposure. Weakness: a synthesis of heterogeneous reviews with no pooled estimates, so direction is reported without magnitude, and the included reviews share primary studies. Relevance: it argues for behaviour-weighted exposure in index design, which in practice means personal or microenvironment sensing rather than a single station value.

PAPERS.title: Saharan dust transport and boundary layer entrainment over western Europe: multi-instrument observations and convection-permitting model evaluation
PAPERS.short: Four Saharan dust events over southwest Germany: ICON-ART within 20 min and 50 m of observed arrival; re-initialization lifts near-surface PM correlation from 0.65-0.69 to 0.86-0.88
PAPERS.pm: Lidar depolarization-separated dust backscatter, sun photometer AOD, in situ aerosol size distributions, satellite observations; near-surface PM
PAPERS.endpoint: Dust vertical structure, boundary-layer entrainment and model skill
PAPERS.affil: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany; Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, Germany
PAPERS.n: Four contrasting Saharan dust events over southwestern Germany evaluated with ground lidar, sun photometer, in situ aerosol measurements, satellites, back trajectories and convection-permitting ICON-ART, including an outbreak with AOD near 1.4. A depolarization method separated dust from other aerosol for like-for-like comparison. ICON-ART reproduced arrival times to about 20 min and layer heights to about 50 m; daily re-initialization raised correlation with observed near-surface PM from 0.65-0.69 to 0.86-0.88, with 2 and 1 km resolution helping mainly in combination with re-initialization. The model overestimated 0.5-2 um particles and underestimated those above 2 um. Weakness: four events at one site, and no CIs on the correlation gains. Relevance: the size-dependent bias is the error any sensor-based dust product inherits, since optical sensors mis-size coarse particles the same way.

PAPERS.title: An Innovative Ion Chromatography Method for Determination of Hydroxymethanesulfonate (HMS) in Ambient Air
PAPERS.short: Peroxide-based differential ion chromatography for particulate hydroxymethanesulfonate: 97.5% conversion, 99.6% filter recovery, MDL 0.018 mg/L; archived filters lose ~25% of HMS in a month
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 filter samples (~180) from a rural North China Plain site; HMS quantified indirectly as sulfate after H2O2 conversion
PAPERS.endpoint: Hydroxymethanesulfonate measurement accuracy and ambient concentrations
PAPERS.affil: Zhejiang University of Technology, China; Research Center for Eco-Environmental Sciences, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China
PAPERS.n: A hydrogen-peroxide differential ion chromatography method quantifies particulate hydroxymethanesulfonate indirectly via the stable sulfate signal. Under optimized conditions (H2O2:HMS >= 4:1, 60 C, 30 min) conversion reached 97.5 +/- 0.3%, spiked-filter recovery 99.6 +/- 1.4% over 0.025-10 mg/L, with a method detection limit of 0.018 mg/L. In ~180 PM2.5 samples from a rural North China Plain site, autumn HMS averaged 0.59 +/- 0.70 ug/m3 (maximum 3.75) and matched or exceeded winter values, tracking high humidity and formaldehyde; archived filters lost about 25% of HMS within a month, implying historical data are biased low. Weakness: single site, indirect quantification that assumes complete and specific conversion, and no inter-laboratory check. Relevance: a storage artefact of this size is a reminder that filter-based reference data used to calibrate sensors carry their own drift.

PAPERS.title: Drivers of Regional Aerosol pH Differences over Eastern China Quantified with a Thermodynamic Framework
PAPERS.short: WRF-GC coupled to E-AIM: wintertime aerosol pH 2.54-4.32 across six eastern China regions; temperature drives 58-63% of the deviation in southern regions, ammonia 41-58% in high-emission ones
PAPERS.pm: Modelled wintertime PM composition and thermodynamic aerosol pH over six regions of eastern China; ammonia gas-particle partitioning framework
PAPERS.endpoint: Regional aerosol pH, its drivers and response to ammonia reduction
PAPERS.affil: Nankai University, China; Nankai University, China
PAPERS.n: WRF-GC coupled with the Extended Aerosol Inorganics Model computes wintertime aerosol pH across six eastern Chinese regions and decomposes regional differences through ammonia gas-particle partitioning. Monthly mean pH spans 2.54-4.32, more acidic in the south. Temperature contributes 58-63% of the regional deviation in the Yangtze River Delta, Pearl River Delta and northeast plain, while ammonia dominates (41-58%) in the high-emission North China and Fenwei plains; negative covariance among drivers damps intramonthly variation. Sensitivity to ammonia reduction rises sharply in ammonia-poor regimes, so large cuts would acidify aerosol more than linearly. Weakness: no observational pH constraint, and pH is not directly measurable, so the result is model-internal. Relevance: aerosol acidity governs secondary formation and metal solubility - properties that drive health effects but are invisible to any mass-based monitor.

PAPERS.title: Particle removal by wet spraying scrubbers: an experimental study in a municipal waste incineration plant.
PAPERS.short: Downscaled wet spray scrubber on incinerator flue gas: >90% removal of 0.3-7 um particles with 97 um droplets and 10 L/m3 liquid-to-gas; contact time 4-10 s irrelevant
PAPERS.pm: Inlet and outlet particle mass and number size distributions (mode ~0.3 um), metal and carbon content, oxidative potential, SEM morphology
PAPERS.endpoint: Fractional particle removal efficiency of a wet spraying scrubber
PAPERS.affil: not stated; not stated
PAPERS.n: A downscaled wet spraying scrubber fed with a slipstream of municipal waste incinerator flue gas was run under nine operating conditions, with particle mass and number measured upstream and downstream and fractional efficiencies computed from number size distributions. Most particles were submicron (mode ~0.3 um) with carbon below 1 wt% and Na and K near 10 wt% each; larger particles carried more metal and higher oxidative potential. Removal exceeded 90% for 0.3-7 um particles with small droplets (nominal D32 97 um) and a high liquid-to-gas ratio (10 L/m3), while gas-spray contact time between 4 and 10 s had no observed effect. Weakness: a downscaled unit on a flue-gas fraction, nine conditions without replication statistics, and no CIs. Relevance: submicron modes with composition-dependent oxidative potential are the fraction optical sensors size worst.
